reasons: No tests for these shapes were found in the packet.
The article status types do not match the database statuses.
The event ID types differ between records.

terms.meaning: a library that checks data has the right shape, types, and values when it is created
a fixed list of allowed values, such as the only valid sectors
the automatic check that data follows its rules before it is used
a description of a record's fields and their rules
a long unique identifier, generated automatically to tell records apart

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setting up data model imports
sections.what: Brings in date and identifier tools, plus the Pydantic library that checks data has the right shape and values.
sections.why: Pydantic is used so bad data is caught when it is created, before it reaches the database.
sections.watch_out: The field validator decorators need a recent Pydantic version, and older versions will fail to load this file.

sections.name: Sector
sections.title: Allowed project sectors
sections.what: A fixed list of sectors a project can belong to, such as Energy, Transport, or Water.
sections.why: A fixed list keeps labels consistent, so filters and reports match.
sections.watch_out: Adding a sector means updating this list and any database or screen values that depend on it.

sections.name: ProjectStatus
sections.title: Allowed project lifecycle stages
sections.what: Lists where a project stands, from announced through construction to operational, delayed, or cancelled.
sections.why: Keeps status labels consistent across the app.
sections.watch_out: New projects start as announced unless another status is set.

sections.name: StageMilestone
sections.title: Allowed event milestone types
sections.what: Lists the kinds of milestone a news event can describe, such as a request for proposals, a final investment decision, or commissioning.
sections.why: Keeps event types consistent across the app.
sections.watch_out: An event fails validation before saving if the AI returns a milestone that is not on this list.

sections.name: StakeholderRole
sections.title: Allowed stakeholder roles
sections.what: Lists the roles a company can play in a project, such as owner, developer, operator, contractor, financier, or regulator.
sections.why: Keeps role labels consistent across the app.
sections.watch_out: A company whose role is not on this list, such as consultant, will fail validation.

sections.name: ConfidenceLevel
sections.title: Allowed confidence labels
sections.what: Three labels describing how sure the system is about a stakeholder: high, medium, or low.
sections.why: Keeps confidence labels consistent.
sections.watch_out: The medium label is stored as the short text med, so any filter must use that exact text.

sections.name: Location
sections.title: Place of a project or event
sections.what: Holds a country and optional region, latitude, and longitude, and rejects coordinates outside the valid range.
sections.why: Likely reason: the checks stop impossible map positions from being stored.
sections.watch_out: Coordinates are optional, so the map must skip places that have none.

sections.name: Capex
sections.title: Money spent on a project
sections.what: Holds the stated amount, its currency, and the amount converted to US dollars, all optional.
sections.why: Many news items give no figure, so every field is allowed to be empty.
sections.watch_out: Nothing checks that the converted US dollar value matches the stated amount and currency.

sections.name: Capacity
sections.title: Size of a project
sections.what: Holds one size measurement and its unit, such as MW, km, or beds.
sections.why: Projects are measured in different units, so the unit is stored with the number.
sections.watch_out: The unit is free text rather than a fixed list, so spelling variants such as MW and mw are both accepted.

sections.name: Source
sections.title: Where a news item came from
sections.what: Holds the web address, language, and outlet name of a source article.
sections.why: Lets a reader check the original report.
sections.watch_out: The language defaults to English even if the article is in another language.

sections.name: Company
sections.title: Company details
sections.what: Holds a company name and an optional stock ticker.
sections.why: Reusable record for owners, developers, and similar parties.
sections.watch_out: The ticker is not checked against any list of real market symbols.

sections.name: Project
sections.title: Capital project record
sections.what: Describes one project with its name, alternate names, sector, country, location, owners, status, and first and last seen dates.
sections.why: Likely reason: a central record that news events attach to.
sections.watch_out: No function in the code shown builds this model, and the database stores projects separately, so changes here may not reach the database.

sections.name: Stakeholder
sections.title: A company's role in an event
sections.what: Holds a stakeholder's role, company name, optional ticker, a written reason, and a confidence label.
sections.why: Records who did what in an event and how sure the system is.
sections.watch_out: The written reason is required, so the AI output must always include one.

sections.name: ProjectEvent
sections.title: One news event about a project
sections.what: The main record for a single news event. It holds the English title and summary, milestone, date, money, size, places, stakeholders, three scores from 0 to 1, sources, cluster keys, notes, and timestamps.
sections.why: Keeps everything about one event in one structure.
sections.watch_out: Each of the three scores must be between 0 and 1, and a value outside that range rejects the whole event.

sections.name: EventizationOutput
sections.title: Container for the first AI step
sections.what: Wraps the list of events returned by the first AI step, called eventization.
sections.why: Checks the AI output has the expected shape before it is used.
sections.watch_out: One malformed event makes the whole list fail validation.

sections.name: StakeholderImpact
sections.title: Stakeholders for one event
sections.what: Links an event ID with its list of stakeholders, as produced by the second AI step.
sections.why: Lets the stakeholder results be matched back to the events they belong to.
sections.watch_out: The event ID is plain text here but a UUID in the event record, so the two must be converted before matching.

sections.name: StakeholderMappingOutput
sections.title: Container for the second AI step
sections.what: Holds the list of stakeholder groups produced by the second AI step.
sections.why: Checks the AI output has the expected shape.
sections.watch_out: One malformed group makes the whole list fail validation.

sections.name: EventScore
sections.title: Scores for one event
sections.what: Holds the three 0 to 1 scores for one event, plus a written justification, from the third AI step.
sections.why: Makes sure the AI scores are in range and come with an explanation.
sections.watch_out: Scores outside 0 to 1 are rejected.

sections.name: ScoringOutput
sections.title: Container for the third AI step
sections.what: Holds the list of event scores produced by the third AI step.
sections.why: Checks the AI output has the expected shape.
sections.watch_out: One bad score makes the whole list fail validation.

sections.name: UIText
sections.title: Text shown on the map for one event
sections.what: Holds a short map pin label, a tooltip, and a card summary for one event.
sections.why: Keeps map labels short and consistent.
sections.watch_out: Pin labels longer than 60 characters are rejected, so AI output must stay short.

sections.name: UIOutput
sections.title: Container for map text
sections.what: Holds the list of map text items for a batch of events.
sections.why: Checks the shape of the AI output for the map.

sections.name: RawNewsItem
sections.title: A news article before processing
sections.what: Holds the title, summary, web address, language, publish date, outlet, fetch time, and processing fields for one article.
sections.why: Gives every article one standard shape as it moves through the pipeline.
sections.watch_out: The processed field is a true or false value here, but the database stores text statuses such as pending, skipped, and processed, so the two do not match directly.

sections.name: NewsSource
sections.title: Settings for one news feed
sections.what: Describes a feed with its address, name, category, and whether it is turned on.
sections.why: Describes a feed in the same shape as its entries in the config file.
sections.watch_out: No code in the packet uses this model, so changing it will not change how feeds are read by itself.

summary: Defines the standard shapes for projects, news events, stakeholders, scores, and raw articles, and checks incoming data against them.
purpose: Provides one set of rules for what valid project and news data looks like.
why: Likely reason: AI output and news feeds can be messy, so checking shape early keeps bad data out of the database.
how: 1) Define fixed lists for sectors, stages, roles, and confidence. 2) Define small parts such as location, money, and size. 3) Combine the parts into project, stakeholder, and event records. 4) Define a container for each AI step's output. 5) Define the shapes for raw articles and feed settings. The checks run whenever a record is created.
inputs: Values from news feeds, the AI steps, and the database.
outputs: Checked record objects, or an error that names the field that failed.
risks: Changing an allowed value can break stored data or AI instructions. Scores outside 0 to 1 and coordinates outside range are rejected. The article status types disagree with the database. The event ID is text in one place and a UUID in another.
debug: When a validation error appears, read the field name it names, then compare that field's rules in this file with the AI output or source row that caused it. If errors mention field validators, check the installed Pydantic version.
